MacBook Pro 16-inch M3 Max (Nov 2023, no Ultra variant in 16-inch form)

sources.ref: macOS 27.0 26A428: t6034 is dual-die T6031; j514map.adt and j516map.adt are listed in the 27.0 fetch log but t6034 is not a separate SoC in the arm-io ADT — T6031 j514m/j516m are M3 Max laptops. There is NO M3 Ultra board in 27.0; M3 Ultra did not ship. The t6034 .dtsi exists in the kernel S4 (T6034 is a future-marketing-name SoC that the kernel reserves).
BuildManifest 27.0 lists t6034 j514map/j516map as MacBook Pro M3 Max (no Ultra product). M3 Ultra did not ship in 2023/2024 with macOS 27.0.
aurora-silicon/linux asahi-7.1.13-3; arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple/t6034.dtsi (#include t6031.dtsi), t6034-j514m.dts, t6034-j516m.dts

note: M3 Ultra was never sold. T6034 is a t6031 dual-die SKU reserved by the kernel but has no M3 Ultra board. The closest analog is M2 Ultra (T6022) which is a true dual-die SKU with T6022 j180d/j475d boards (artifacts/AneAllSoc/every-soc/receipt/adt-27.0.txt arm-io,t6020 section: ane1 + dart-ane1 on die 1). The T6034 j514m/j516m 'M3 Ultra' assumption in the lab survey is wrong — these are M3 Max boards. The actual M3 Ultra SKU, if it ships, will be T6034 j7xx-d or similar with two T6031 dies and ane0/ane1/ane2/ane3 (analogous to T6002 ane0/ane1/ane2/ane3).
